items.title: Supergirl Sets Digital Release Date After Disappointing Run in Theaters
items.description: Supergirl debuts in North America on Digital on July 28, after a disappointing run in theaters that saw just $121 million made at the global box office.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Supergirl debuts in North America on Digital on July 28, after a disappointing run in theaters that saw just $121 million made at the global box office.

On July 28, Supergirl will be available at home on participating digital platforms, including Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, Fandango, and more. The DC Universe movie then launches on 4K UHD, Blu-ray, and DVD on September 8.

Supergirl, which stars Milly Alcock in the dual role of Supergirl/Kara Zor-El, followed last year’s DCU kickstarter Superman, but failed to generate anywhere near as much interest from cinemagoers. It was deemed a box office bomb when it debuted to a global total of $68 million following its June 26 premiere. The Warner Bros. superhero movie reportedly had a $170 million production budget and $120 million marketing budget, suggesting the studio would need around $300 million just to break even. Supergirl didn’t come close to that milestone.

"While Supergirl didn’t meet our box office expectations," DC Studios co-CEO Peter Safran told The New York Times following Supergirl's opening weekend, "it’s just one component of a broader, long-term strategy at DC Studios that we remain confident in."

To that end, Lanterns is set to premiere on HBO Max in August, Clayface comes out in October, then Superman follow-up Man of Tomorrow hits theaters in 2027.

Alcock will play a significant role in Man of Tomorrow and beyond, DC Studios has said. Supergirl takes place after the events of Superman and sees her encounter other galactic characters like Lobo, played by Jason Momoa. As for Man of Tomorrow, all we really know about the movie is that Superman and supervillain Lex Luthor have to work together to combat the threat of Brainiac. But we can also expect to see the main cast from Superman return. With Supergirl’s involvement, could we see the Justice League finally take shape?

For more, you can check out IGN's 6/10 Supergirl review. You can also read about some behind-the-scenes details that suggest creative differences between DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn and director Craig Gillespie impacted the final product.

Supergirl Digital, 4K UHD, and Blu-ray contain over 90 minutes of bonus features including the following:

  • The Making of Supergirl Consider Supergirl a “Hero’s Journey” for Milly Alcock. She transformed throughout the process of leading her first feature film. We watch as a fly-on-the-wall during key moments of production.
  • Flying Off the Page Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow, written by Tom King with art by Bilquis Evely, was the jumping off point for DC to adapt Supergirl into a film. We follow the comic authors, screenwriter Ana Nogueira, and filmmakers, as they make the leap from page to screen.
  • Space is a Bad Neighborhood, Babe Explore with Production Designer Neil Lamont, as he takes us through the many worlds that Kara Zor-El steps into on her journey to hunt down Krem of the Yellow Hills.
  • A Practical Legacy There are so many aliens and unique looks in this film that are literally out of this world! Legacy Effects and Peter Swords King explain the creative process behind this diverse group of creatures.
  • Showdown at Evely Square Production spent a month filming this action set-piece. From stunt training, to crashing tanks, to classic superhero flying moments, this breaks down the making of an incredible action scene.
  • The DC Dream: Lobo Jason Momoa has been outspoken over wanting to play Lobo for years, and now his time has come. Go behind the scenes as he transforms into this iconic and chaotic character.
  • Mixtape for a Hero What does Supergirl, as a character, sound like? Director Craig Gillespie and Composer Claudia Sarne answer this question as they discuss the score for the film.
  • You Are Here: A Supergirl Map of the Galaxy If you want to know more about all the planets visited in the film, check out this piece, narrated by Ruthye herself, actress Eve Ridley, to learn some more details, and enjoy the alien aesthetic of the film up close!
  • Girl's Best Friend Krypto is Kara’s badly-behaved BFF and last connection to her home world of Krypton. We delve into their relationship and what makes it so special.
  • Krypto Saves the Day: Coastal Catastrophe An animated short that tells the story of a fun day at the beach which goes sideways when some sneaky foes get between Krypto and his hot dog.
  • Deleted Scenes

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Disgaea Creator Slams Sony for Scrapping Discs, Says PlayStation Might as Well 'Go All the Way' and Scrap Consoles Too
items.description: Disgaea creator and former Nippon Ichi Software CEO Sohei Niikawa has criticized Sony’s decision to ditch physical games, and said that the executives responsible didn't "understand the feelings" of impacted fans.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Disgaea creator and former Nippon Ichi Software CEO Sohei Niikawa has criticized Sony’s decision to ditch physical games, and said that the executives responsible didn't "understand the feelings" of impacted fans.

Earlier this month, Sony announced that from January 2028 onwards it will no longer produce disc releases of new games. This decision triggered huge backlash online, with fans even expressing their anger at Sony in the comments on trailers for unrelated upcoming third party games.

Noisy Pixel interviewed Niikawa at Anime Expo 2026, where he was promoting his upcoming game, Demons’ Night Fever, which describes itself as a speedrun-training simulation RPG. He also gave his opinion on Sony’s move to ditch physical disc releases.

"From a purely business perspective, I can understand why the people at Sony would make that decision.” said Niikawa, who was CEO of Nippon Ichi Software between 2009 to 2022. “However, the executives who decided it have probably never experienced coming to an event like Anime Expo and having someone approach them with a physical game to ask for an autograph. I don’t think they understand the feelings of those fans, and they may never have considered what physical editions mean to the people who value them."

Nikawa then added that "If they’re going to go as far as eliminating physical packages, they may as well eliminate the hardware too. A television would be enough. Why would you need the console? If you’re going to get rid of physical games, you may as well go all the way."

Sony’s digital game sales have been on the rise for years, far outselling physical releases. For example, just 7 PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies in the US so far this year. Sony have framed their decision to stop releasing discs as following current PS4 and PS5 owners’ behavior. In the announcement on the official PlayStation blog, Sony framed phasing out discs as "a natural direction” for Sony as the company is adapting "to consumer trends as the general preference for digital media significantly outpaces physical discs."

Despite this trend, the backlash shows that physical media, especially the act of owning a game on a disc, is still very important to many. As Niikawa referenced, there is the importance of having something physical to put on your shelf. However, a disc-less box with a download code inside just doesn’t cut it for many, as shown by the backlash to GTA6’s physical release.

From conservationists’ point of view, games getting a disc release that only contains part of the game (see 007: First Light for a recent example) or which require a patch download to function properly has been a growing issue in both the PS4 and PS5 generations. This calls into question whether there is any value at all in having a physical game that can’t even be played without a download from a server.

Others in the Japanese game industry have also weighed in on Sony’s decision, with many raising concerns about the risks to game ownership and preservation in a digital-only future. Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima expressed concern about how access to digital content can easily be withdrawn, removing the purchaser’s ability to own and use it when they wish. More recently, Kojima said of Sony’s decision that "I grew up with physical media, so I find it really sad." Nier creator Yoko Taro also echoed these sentiments in a recent tweet where he urged people to buy physical game releases while they still can.

Sony’s statements point clearly to games being digital only on the upcoming PS6, which is likely to be some kind of hybrid console/handheld, if comments from Sony CEO Nishino are anything to go by. It’s still unclear whether Sony will offer some kind of disc drive add-on that will enable gamers to play their discs from previous generations, or whether physical game collectors will just have to stick with older hardware.

Going forward, it seems that true physical games (where everything is actually in the box and ready to play) could become a niche, expensive product, only released in limited quantities by companies like Super Rare and Limited Run, who have a long track record of re-releasing physical games on various platforms.

This week, it was claimed that Sony knew its decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs would spark outrage, and reportedly has issued staff with the "strictest" social media guidelines to stop them from publicly commenting on the controversy.

Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

items.title: 'She's Not in This Movie': Tom Holland Insists Jean Grey Won't Appear in Spider-Man: Brand New Day — So Is He Lying, or Is Sadie Sink Really Playing Someone Else?
items.description: With just a week to go until the launch of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Tom Holland has stunned fans by stating that X-Men hero Jean Grey is "not in this movie" — despite months of rumors that this is who Sadie Sink is playing.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
With just a week to go until the launch of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Tom Holland has stunned fans by stating that X-Men hero Jean Grey is "not in this movie" — despite months of rumors that this is who Sadie Sink is playing.

Brand New Day's buildup has been dominated by speculation over who Sink has been cast as, with an array of possible names initially in the mix. But, over time, insider whispers and fan discussion have coalesced around Jean Grey — to the point that if it now is anyone but her, many moviegoers would be floored.

Still, nothing is official. Which is why it's even more surprising that Holland has now responded to a comment about Jean Grey during a recent interview. Rather than decline to say anything further, the Spider-Man star instead took the opportunity to bluntly deny that the X-Men member would appear.

"Jean Grey can help her," stated Brazilian TikToker Natalia Kreuser, suggesting that the superhero's psychic powers could help recover MJ's lost memories of Peter Parker. "She's not in this movie but it would be pretty cool," Holland responded.

‘Oh she’s not in this movie, but that would be pretty cool’ - Tom Holland when asked if Jean Grey would help Peter Parker.

He says this while trying to hide a smile, cheeky 😉 😂 pic.twitter.com/KSkeuDhxnc

— SukunaOnFN (@SukunaOnFN1) July 23, 2026

Is Holland playing coy? There's seemingly no way to interpret his remark as anything other than a flat denial of Jean Grey being in the movie — which would, as we've said, be a big surprise at this point.

Or, is Holland now employing the Andrew Garfield trick of straight-up misdirecting fans? After months of being asked whether he was in Spider-Man: No Way Home, Garfield began flatly denying that — though, of course, he was indeed present.

Last year, it was reported that Sink will be back in 2027's climactic Multiverse Saga finale Avengers: Secret Wars, something that seemingly sets her up for a far bigger MCU role. Of course, Marvel is currently prepping its big X-Men reboot, which is being helmed by Thunderbolts/The New Avengers director Jake Schreier. Introducing Jean Grey now would allow Marvel to gently introduce audiences to the idea of a fresh generation of X-Men, before fans get to say farewell to various legacy characters who are returning for Avengers: Doomsday.

Speaking on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Sink discussed the huge amount of secrecy over her role and described not being able to say who she's playing as "torture." Subsequent trailers have kept Sink in the shadows, though she has now begun giving interviews on Spider-Man: Brand New Day's promotional tour, with rather amusingly tight-lipped results.

Beyond a marketing tactic to get fans speculating, director Destin Daniel Cretton has insisted that fans will ultimately appreciate being kept in suspense, and stated that Marvel was keeping the identity of Sadie Sink's character a secret until fans see the movie for a "very real reason" that he believes fans won't "get mad at."

Whatever the truth is, there's thankfully now just one week to go until we finally find out — as Spider-Man: Brand New Day opens in theaters on July 31.

Image credit: James McCauley/Variety via Getty Images

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Scott Pilgrim Creator Bryan Lee O'Malley Returns to the Series for the First New Comic in 16 Years | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Oni Press has revealed that Scott Pilgrim creator Bryan Lee O'Malley is returning to the series for its first new comic in 16 years.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
Scott Pilgrim creator Bryan Lee O'Malley may have ended his beloved saga 16 years ago with the release of Scott Pilgrim's Finest Hour, but it seems he's still not quite done. Today at Comic-Con, Oni Press announced a new Scott Pilgrim comic called Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott.

As first revealed by Gizmodo, Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott is a one-shot prequel to the recently released beat-em-up game Scott Pilgrim EX (which also makes this a sequel to the animated series Scott Pilgrim Takes Off). Check out a short preview of the issue in the slideshow gallery below:

Here's the official description for Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott:

Scott met Ramona. Sparks flew. The two of them had to work together in order to defeat Ramona’s Seven Evil Exes and their nefarious leader, Gideon Gordon Graves. Some other stuff happened in various media formats that may or may not be canon. That’s all in the past. These days, Scott and Ramona are a happy couple, and the Exes have moved on from their unhealthy obsessions. I guess they all got therapy or whatever. Now, after a period of peace, a new threat is about to emerge. Are our heroes ready? Let’s find out!!!

“When I was asked to create a minicomic for Scott Pilgrim EX, I quickly said yes without considering the implications,” O’Malley said in a statement. “Only when I started writing and drawing it did I realize this would be the first new Scott Pilgrim comic in 16 years. It’s only a trifle, but returning to Scott’s Toronto really did feel like coming home.”

Scott Pilgrim EX: Dawn of Metal Scott will be released on November 15. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop.

In IGN's Scott Pilgrim EX review, Will Borger writes, "Scott Pilgrim EX is the latest in a long line of retro revivals from Tribute Games, and like all of its previous works, the developer has done an admirable job of producing a beat ‘em up that builds on its predecessor while adding much appreciated gameplay depth and plenty of replayability. I love EX’s RPG systems (simple as they are), its world, and how there is always another interesting character to try when I get bored. But it’s also a game that grapples with the passage of time, even if it perhaps doesn’t mean to. The modern beat ‘em up exists because of the games that came before, but they were often far more limited. With the passage of time, we’ve returned to those ideas and refined them. Like Scott Pilgrim itself, those games have gone from something that was new to something that is now referenced. Nostalgia is a powerful drug, but a bittersweet one, and Scott Pilgrim EX understands that. You can go back in time, but you can’t go back to the way things were. All that’s left is to appreciate where you’ve been and enjoy what’s here now. And you know what? What’s here is pretty fun."

You can also check out IGN's full SDCC 2026 schedule.

items.title: Marvel's Wolverine: Deep Cuts SDCC Panel Live Report | Comic Con 2026
items.description: Our San Diego Comic-Con 2026 live reporting kicks off with Insomniac’s panel for upcoming PlayStation 5 exclusive, Marvel’s Wolverine.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
San Diego Comic-Con 2026 is here, and IGN is at the show reporting live on all the panels that matter.

Our live reporting kicks off with Insomniac’s panel for upcoming PlayStation 5 exclusive, Marvel’s Wolverine, which begins at 11.15am PT / 2.15pm ET / 7.15pm UK time direct from Hall H. There, Insomniac Games’ creative director Marcus Smith, game director Mike Daly, narrative director Walt Williams, and senior project director Jess Reiner-Reed, alongside actors Liam McIntyre (Wolverine) and Krizia Bajos (Jean Grey), as well well as executive producer Eric Monacelli from Marvel Games, will unveil new details from the game. items.title: Microsoft Launches Test for Ad-Supported Xbox Game Streaming, Promises the Ads Will Not 'Interrupt the Flow of Gameplay'
items.description: Ad-supported Xbox game streaming is here, Microsoft has said. Here's how it works and how you can try it out.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Microsoft has launched a test for ad-supported Xbox game streaming, and promised the ads won't interrupt gameplay.

The test lets users stream select games from their library for a limited time supported by adverts, and is available to Xbox Insiders. During this test period, Xbox Insiders with an Xbox account can stream supported games without a subscription for free with ads, with one-hour session limits across supported devices and regions where game streaming is available.

Ads will play before streaming sessions begin and will not interrupt gameplay, Microsoft insisted. The core game experience remains unchanged, the company added. Participation is optional, and players can choose other ways to play at any time.

The test is designed to help give more people more affordable ways to play on devices they already own, Microsoft explained. You can play after sitting through two minutes of ads. When your 1-hour session ends, you can play again after sitting through another set of ads, and your progress continues across your account and devices. It's also worth noting that today, Xbox Cloud Gaming is not available without a Game Pass subscription.

“For many players, the device they already own now allows them to stream games with Xbox,” Microsoft said. “Cloud can also help Xbox One owners play newer games built for Xbox Series X|S without needing to purchase new hardware right away. That can be especially meaningful in places where consoles are harder to find or less affordable, giving more players another way to access great games on devices they already have.

“Advertising has existed in gaming for decades, from in-game placements to free-to-play models. But it hasn’t always been built with the player in mind. When done well, advertising can help lower the cost of access. It creates another way for players to get into games without an upfront streaming purchase and expands audiences through new ways to play.

“For brands, this only works if showing up here adds to the experience, not takes away from it.”

In a blog post on Xbox Wire, Microsoft outlined the following guidelines for ad-supported game streaming:

  1. We start with the player. Ads should create value.
  2. We do not interrupt the flow of gameplay.
  3. We hold ads to the same quality bar as our content.
  4. We’re clear about what’s advertising.
  5. We make sure ads fit what players expect on each platform.

Microsoft said it will learn from the test and improve it based on feedback.

The test of ad-supported Xbox game streaming arrives amid console price rises that are pushing some gaming hardware towards the $1,000 mark. Last month, Microsoft announced significant price rises for Xbox consoles, blaming the ongoing “components crisis.” In a blog post, Microsoft said that from August 1, the price of Xbox consoles will increase by $100 for 512GB models, and $150 for 1TB models. The 2TB model will be discontinued.

Xbox console price rises June 2026:

  • Xbox Series S 512GB: $399.99 —> $499.99
  • Xbox Series S 1TB: $449.99 —> $599.99
  • Xbox Series X 1TB Digital: $599.99 —> $749.99
  • Xbox Series X 1TB: $649.99 —> $799.99

“Last October, we increased Xbox console price by $20-$70 in the U.S.” Microsoft said at the time. “We hoped another price increase would not be necessary, and we have spent the last several months working with suppliers on options. Unfortunately, console storage and memory prices have increased by more than 2.5x and we expect another doubling by the fall of 2027.

"The entire consumer electronics industry is struggling with the current components crisis, but the effects are particularly hard on consoles. Unlike phones, computers, speakers, and other consumer devices, consoles are typically not sold at a profit, but instead for less than they cost to make.”

New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has said the spiralling cost of new and existing consoles would require "radically different business models" over the coming generation. She added that the industry had "reached a point where it will be hard to imagine" mass audiences still being able to afford "thousands of dollars" for a new console generation.

The current PS5 and Xbox Series X and S generation of consoles have seen price increases rather than cost savings. Sony itself raised the price of PS5 consoles back in March, blaming “continued pressures in the global economic landscape.” Nintendo has also not been immune, and recently acknowledged it would up the price of Switch 2, just over a year after its arrival. And Valve has bemoaned its struggle to release Steam Machine at the price it had initially hoped, instead having to go for an eye-watering $1,049.

With this context, it's easy to see why Microsoft would want to introduce ad-supported Xbox game streaming now. I imagine Sharma also has an eye on the response to the test ahead of any potential introduction of ad-supported gaming on the non-streaming side.

The test also comes amid what Sharma has called the most significant restructure in Xbox history. 1,600 staff were cut from Microsoft’s gaming business earlier this month, with another 1,600 to go over the current financial year. Four studios have left the business, with another on the way out.

“Our business today is not healthy,” Sharma said. “We are operating at margins that are 3-10x lower than comparable platform and publishing businesses. We entered Gen 9 with a smaller install base and a higher cost structure. To grow, we bet on Game Pass, multi-platform, and a broader portfolio of content. While those businesses have created meaningful value, they did not grow at the pace we expected. As that happened, our core business weakened, and we added more teams, more investment, and more time, hoping for a better outcome. And now the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in its history. We must reset Xbox.”

Yesterday, Microsoft announced Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC, allowing you to play classic console games on PC and handhelds such as the Xbox Ally X for the first time.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Former Assassin's Creed, Watch Dogs Director Likens Large-Scale Game Development to Working With 'Flaming Barrels Falling Down From a Construction Site,' Months After Parting Ways With Ubisoft
items.description: Watch Dogs and Splinter Cell veteran Clint Hocking has described the experience of leading a large team within Ubisoft as like working while "flaming barrels [are] falling down from a construction site," akin to a scene from Donkey Kong.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Watch Dogs and Splinter Cell development veteran Clint Hocking has described the experience of leading a large team within Ubisoft as like working while "flaming barrels [are] falling down from a construction site," akin to a scene from the arcade game Donkey Kong.

Hocking made the comment as part of a lengthy discussion about how his role changed as development team sizes grew, leading him to feel less effective while leading Ubisoft's multi-studio effort on Watch Dogs Legion.

Hocking and Ubisoft parted ways abruptly earlier this year amid a reshuffle at the top of the publisher's prized Assassin's Creed brand, despite being in the middle of leading development on Assassin's Creed Hexe. The franchise's next blockbuster, Hexe is understood to still be on target to arrive in 2027.

"On [Splinter Cell] Chaos Theory, I would just walk over to the desk of the person who was making a thing, and sit down with them and talk to them about what they're doing," Hocking recalled, speaking via the FRVR podcast.

"We could have a conversation," he continued, suggesting a scenario where he was able to offer granular input such as the placement of a specific light source to better guide player movement.

"But on a huge game with 1,000 people, you go into a meeting to review some piece of content — some quest, say, or some location — and there's 30 people in the meeting," Hocking continued. "Directors and producers and project managers, and very often even the level designer who built it isn't even in the meeting.

"And it's like, 'where's the person who worked on this?' 'Ah, they're working on the thing they need to do for their next meeting. But don't worry we'll take notes and put it in Jira for them.' So there's people there writing down what you say, making tasks of it.

"Then you finish the review, you say, 'OK, when are we going to see the iterations and the improvements we talked about?' And they're like, 'Well... so it's going to be six weeks before we see an iteration on this because the person who needs to do the iteration is working on this [other thing].' Then, by the time you get back there six weeks later, maybe the whole context is different. It very often feels like... you know those flaming barrels that Donkey Kong throws down at you? Very often game development feels like this stream of burning barrels falling down from a construction site."

Hocking initially joined Ubisoft to work on the legendary 2002 stealth action adventure Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell, which he contributed to as a designer and scriptwriter. Hocking then served as creative director on its follow-up, Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory, before holding the same role on Far Cry 2.

During a period away from Ubisoft, Hocking served years at LucasArts, Valve, and Amazon. Hocking then returned to Ubisoft to serve once again as a creative director, this time on Watch Dogs: Legion, which launched in 2020 to a mixed response. Following that, Hocking moved over to Assassin's Creed, and had been leading work on Hexe out of the company's Montreal studio. Legion remains Hocking's only shipped title since Far Cry 2 back in 2008.

Hocking's role leading Assassin's Creed Hexe has now been taken up by Jean Guesdon, the Assassin's Creed franchise's Head of Content, who is seen as a steady and experience hand with a lengthy track record working on numerous titles in the series.

Photo by ROBYN BECK/AFP via Getty Images.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: The Most Anticipated Movies and TV Shows From San Diego Comic-Con | Comic Con 2026
items.description: From Marvel’s long-awaited return to Hall H ahead of Avengers: Doomsday, to new looks at The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, Blade Runner 2099, Lanterns, Carrie, Star Trek: Strange New Worlds, and much more, here are our most anticipated movies and TV shows at San Diego Comic-Con 2026!
items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:
San Diego Comic-Con is one of the biggest events in the world of entertainment, and it’s set to reveal new looks and deep dives into our favorite movies and TV shows, including those that are some of our most anticipated of the year.

From Marvel’s long-awaited return to Hall H ahead of Avengers: Doomsday, to new looks at The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, Blade Runner 2099, Lanterns, Carrie, Star Trek: Strange New Worlds, and much more, there is a lot to look forward to. We’re here to share what we are most excited about for SDCC!

IGN will be on the ground at SDCC, covering all the biggest news as it happens, alongside hosting two days of livestreams with exclusive reveals, interviews, and more.

Percy Jackson and the Olympians (July 23 at 10am PT)

Season 3 of Percy Jackson and the Olympians is set to debut on Disney+ on November 20, and fans will get an exclusive first look at the new episodes during SDCC. Cast and crew from Percy Jackson and the Olympians will be on hand, and they’ll also chat behind-the-scenes stories, talk about new characters, and preview what it will be like when the Titan’s Curse is brought to life.

Marvel’s Wolverine: Deep Cuts (July 23 at 12pm PT)

We know it isn’t a film or TV show, but we can’t wait for Marvel’s Wolverine on PS5, and SDCC is going to give us a sneak (snikt?!) peek at the upcoming game from Insomniac that will be released on September 15, 2026. We'll also be live reporting from the panel right here.

Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender (July 23 at 2pm PT)

The voice cast and creative team behind Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender will dive deep into the making of this new Paramount+ film that had a major leak and was once set for the big screen. The much-anticipated film will be released on July 25, and you can read our review right now.

Stuart Fails to Save the Universe (July 23 at 2:15pm PT)

The Big Bang Theory spin-off called Stuart Fails to Save the Universe will have an exclusive advance screening at SDCC, and that will be followed by a panel with the cast and crew of the HBO Max series that will also premiere later that day on July 23.

Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2 Advanced Screening and Q&A with Cast and Crew (July 23 at 3:30pm PT)

Ahead of its premiere on July 31 on Prime Video, the first episode of Batman: Caped Crusader Season 2 will be taking center stage at SDCC. The screening will be followed by a Q&A with the voice cast and creative team of the animated noir series. We enjoyed the first season, as we gave it a 7/10 and said: “Batman: Caped Crusader isn’t Batman: The Animated Series, but it does apply its spirit to a captivating detective story.”

Onslaught (July 23 at 5:30pm PT)

Adam Wingard and Simon Barrett’s Onslaught is headed to SDCC, and we’ll get a new look at the film. It’s about an army sniper who must protect a young daughter from a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers who break loose in the desert, and we’ll find out more on July 23.

Blade Runner 2099 (July 24 at 10am PT)

Prime Video is ready to share an exclusive new look at Blade Runner 2099 with a panel featuring the cast and executive producers. They’ll reveal more of the series that continues the franchise that began with 1982’s Blade Runner and its sequel, 2017’s Blade Runner 2049. The series is set to premiere in 2027 with leads Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power (July 24 at 10am PT)

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power is returning for its third season on November 11, and fans will get an exclusive look at the new episodes as well as hearing from the cast and executive producers. This is a big one, as this season will be when we’ll witness Sauron making the One Ring!

Adventure Time: Side Quests (July 24 at 11am PT)

Get ready for more of Finn the Human and Jake the Dog as Adventure Time: Side Quests is on its way. SDCC will provide a fresh look at the brand-new series, now streaming on Hulu and Disney+ in the U.S.

The Walking Dead: Dead City (July 24 at 11:45am PT)

Season 3 of The Walking Dead: Dead City is set to premiere on July 26, and SDCC will feature sneak peeks of the premiere episode and a chat with the cast and producers of the spin-off that stars Jeffrey Dean Morgan and Lauren Cohan. While you wait, you can read our review of The Walking Dead: Dead City Season 3 right now.

The Vampire Lestat (July 24 at 12:30pm PT)

The lastest season of The Vampire Lestat, fka Interview with the Vampire, has just come to an end, and the cast and producers of the series will be on hand to discuss the big finale. For more, we had a chance to speak to showrunner Rolin Jones about the finale, and you can read that here.

Lanterns (July 24 at 1:30pm PT)

A brand-new look at Lanterns is nearly here, as the HBO Max series from co-creators Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King is coming to SDCC. Series stars Kyle Chandler, Aaron Pierre, Garret Dillahunt, and Poorna Jagannathan will also be there to talk about the show and share behind-the-scenes details. Lanterns will debut on HBO Max on August 16.

My Adventures with Superman (July 24 at 2pm PT)

The next chapter of My Adventures with Superman is flying toward us soon, and the cast and creative team will be at SDCC to give a preview of Season 3 and talk about how the show “continues to reimagine the world’s most iconic hero with heart, humor, and action.”

X-Men '97 (July 24 at 2:15pm PT)

We’re currently in the middle of Season 2 of X-Men ’97, but that doesn’t mean the creative team behind the series can’t take a few moments to talk about the show, share stories about its development, and tease what’s to come!

Rick and Morty (July 24 at 3pm PT)

Season 9 of Rick and Morty is currently going strong, and executive producers Dan Harmon and Scott Marder will stop by SDCC to give a deeper look at the current episodes, share behind-the-scenes tales, and discuss what’s next.

King of the Hill (July 24 at 4pm PT)

We gave Season 15 of King of the Hill a 10/10, so you could say we’re excited for this panel with the cast and crew of the series as they share an inside look at this new era of the show and what’s coming for our favorite characters.

Spaceballs: The New One (July 24 at 4pm PT)

Spaceball: The New One is headed to a galaxy near us on April 23, 2027, and SDCC will give us a “behind-the-schwartz” look at the sequel to the 1987 classic.

God of War Laufey: Forging God of War’s Next Heroes (July 24 at 5:30pm PT)

Join the creative team behind the upcoming God of War Laufey as they discuss new details about the anticipated follow-up to 2022’s God of War Ragnarok, including behind-the-scenes insights from development and performance capture.

Dark Matter (July 24 at 10pm PT)

Apple TV and Den of Geek are presenting an exclusive fan screening of the first episode of Dark Matter Season 2, and there will also be special guests on hand, including stars Joel Edgerton and Dayo Okeniyi, creator Blake Crouch, executive producer Matt Tolmach, and producer Jacquelyn Ben-Zekry. Season 2 of Dark Matter will premiere on August 28.

Bob’s Burgers (July 25 at 10am PT)

Join the voice cast and crew of Bob’s Burgers as they talk about what’s been going on with the Belcher family and what may be ahead for them.

Batman: Knightfall Part 1 - Knightfall (July 25 at 10am PT)

Batman: Knightfall Part 1 - Knightfall is an upcoming multi-part animated event that will see Bane freeing Batman’s entire rogues’ gallery from Arkham Asylum. As you can imagine, this isn’t going to go well, and the cast and crew will share more about what fans can expect. Check out our review of Batman: Knightfall Part 1 - Knightfall before it’s released on August 25.

Futurama (July 25 at 11am PT)

In what’s being described as the “wildest Futurama panel since ever,” fans should look forward to getting some world-premiere footage of the new season that will debut on Hulu on August 3, including details on how it came to life.

The Simpsons (July 25 at 11:45am PT)

The Simpsons is back for its “one millionth” time at SDCC, and Matt Groening and other guests will be on hand to present an “exclusive world premiere sneak preview of a chilling new story that challenges everything you thought you knew about Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, Maggie, and Barney.”

Star Trek Universe (July 25 at 12:30pm PT)

While Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4 will take center stage with a premiere on July 23, this Star Trek Universe panel will do so much more; we’ll get a celebration of Star Trek’s 60th anniversary alongside “exclusive footage, major reveals, surprise appearances, and memorable moments.”

items.title: Zach Cregger's New Resident Evil Trailer Includes 2 Cool Details Fans of the Games Will Appreciate
items.description: Today's tense new Resident Evil movie trailer provides our best look yet at Zach Cregger's survival horror adaptation — including a couple more Easter eggs for fans of the games.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Today's tense new Resident Evil movie trailer provides our best look yet at Zach Cregger's survival horror adaptation — including a couple more Easter eggs for fans of the games.

Weapons director Cregger has previously confirmed that his big screen Resident Evil adaptation will stand separate to the games, with familiar characters and plot points left to Capcom's original creations. Instead, his Resident Evil movie will follow its own story and lead character — even if the film will still be littered with references for Resident Evil veterans to appreciate.

Today's trailer includes two more of these, which are not too difficult to spot. But if you haven't watched it yet, here it is to enjoy:

The most obvious Easter egg here is the lingering shot of a typewriter, sitting on a desk in a quiet room. Typewriters are, of course, the Resident Evil game series' typical save mechanic — while the rooms that house them are generally deemed safe from threat. We'll have to see if that holds as true in the movie, but the placement and design of the typewriter here is unmistakably a reference.

Shortly after this, fans will spot a second Easter egg, as lead character Bryan (played by Austin Abrams) scrabbles around in a drawer for ammo. Cregger has previously commented on the fact that this scrounging for supplies is a reference to Capcom's games in itself — as players are rewarded for opening every drawer/cabinet/crate in the hunt for resources. Here in the trailer, though, there's a far more oblique reference: the shotgun shells on offer are clearly the same brand as the one seen in Resident Evil 4.

These Easter eggs follow several more references seen in the movie's first trailer — which Cregger himself pointed out to IGN as part of an exclusive trailer breakdown video. These included a familiar-looking green herb, plus hints at other sequences from the film we're yet to see.

Impressed by how it's looking? Initial reaction to film from some fans featured notable criticism that the movie looked less like a Resident Evil adaptation, and more like a 28 Days Later spinoff. Others, however, praised the fact that Cregger was not rehashing a story that we've all seen previously — and as recently as 2021's poorly-received Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City reboot. Today's look is even more convincing, I feel, with a growing sense of tension, and a better look at Abrams' character as the world around him descends into a zombie apocalypse.

Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie is due to land in theaters on September 18, and we have much more on the film right here on IGN — such as how the director almost killed Abrams in a stunt that's still in the finished movie.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Okay, So We Now Know 1 Weapon Coming to Helldivers 2 as Part of the Warhammer 40,000 Warbond, and I Think We Can Guess a Few Others
items.description: Helldivers 2 will reveal its hotly anticipated Warhammer 40,000 crossover on July 30, Sony has announced. But in the meantime, we have confirmation of one weapon that will be included in the Legendary Warbond.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Helldivers 2 will reveal its hotly anticipated Warhammer 40,000 crossover on July 30, Sony has announced. But in the meantime, we have confirmation of one weapon that will be included in the Legendary Warbond.

The brief teaser video, below, shows a Bolt Pistol, lifted straight from the Warhammer 40,000 armory. Bolt Pistols are used by many different factions and units in Games Workshop’s grimdark far future setting, but it’s particularly fitting in the hands of an Astra Militarum (formerly the Imperial Guard) soldier.

Attention, Helldivers.

July 30 has been designated as a date of operational significance. Update your calendar accordingly.

Further briefing to follow. pic.twitter.com/ekfvkBsWFc

— HELLDIVERS™ 2 (@helldivers2) July 23, 2026

Even before the Warhammer 40,000 crossover was announced, fans had spoken about how it would be the perfect fit for Helldivers 2, which sees groups of four soldiers essentially play the role of cannon fodder in the endless galactic war against horrible alien monsters. You can quite easily equate Helldivers’ alien bug race, the Terminids, to Warhammer 40,000’s Tyranids, for example. The Automatons aren’t a million miles away from the mindless mechanical Necrons, either.

Warhammer 40,000 is something Arrowhead is often asked about in interviews, and by that I mean that I have asked the team about it in interviews because I love this stuff. In April last year, I asked Alex Bolle, production director on Helldivers 2, about a potential Warhammer 40,000 collab, and he said there was discussions being had. "Obviously Warhammer 40,000 is something that a lot of guys internally love to death," he said at the time. "So the devs are discussing, the devs are proposing stuff, and the hype is building. So these are discussions internally that we are having. Warhammer 40,000, I can't really tell you. Maybe. Who knows? We'll see!"

Indeed, in 2024, Arrowhead's Johan Pilestedt published an extended list of IPs he “really would love to do a take on," and Warhammer 40,000 was right up there alongside the likes of Aliens, Starship Troopers, and Terminator.

As for what the Helldivers 2 x Warhammer 40,000 Warbond will include, after the Bolt Pistol reveal we can speculate about what else we’ll see. A Chainsword seems like a safe bet, as does the Astra Militarum’s iconic Lasgun. A Boltgun, however, might be a step too far for Helldivers 2 — it’s usually used by the genetically enhanced super soldiers known as the Space Marines, although there are versions of the Boltgun that can be used by standard humans.

As for armor, I wouldn’t be surprised to see Cadian-style Kasrkin and Scion armor sets for the soldiers of Super Earth. Cadia is one of the most famous planets in the Warhammer 40,000 setting, and its people some of the toughest in the Emperor’s human army. Cadia is no more (that’s a whole thing all its own), but its people live on, as do their wargear.

We’ll find out on July 30.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Luna Is Now Part of Prime Video at No Extra Cost, Amazon Wants to 'Rebuild Trust' in Cloud Gaming
items.description: Amazon has announced that its cloud gaming platform, Luna, is now available on Prime Video — as long as you’re in the U.S. or UK and are using the streaming service on a Fire TV.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Amazon has announced that its cloud gaming platform, Luna, is now available on Prime Video — as long as you’re in the U.S. or UK and are using the streaming service on a Fire TV.

The rollout is part of a wider push from the corporation to get the games that Luna offers into as many hands as possible. Luna is included with Prime at no additional cost, and there’s nothing to download or purchase to start playing.

Amazon said Prime members can find games the same way they discover everything else on Prime Video, just by looking for the new “Games” tab and starting playing in seconds on your TV, using a controller or your phone. On Luna, Prime members get access to a library of games that includes Hogwarts Legacy, EA Sports FC 26, and Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, as well as party games like Clue, Ticket to Ride, and Taboo. Amazon said it plans to add new games ever month.

"For a lot of people, games have been harder to find than they should be,” said Jeff Gattis, GM of Gaming at Amazon. “Bringing Luna inside Prime Video allows Prime members to discover games more naturally, and if they see one they like, they click it, and they’re in. That’s less time searching and more time playing great games included with their Prime membership.”

More details on “additional devices, countries, and games in the months ahead” will be revealed in the future.

IGN spoke to Gattis about this new approach for Luna, cloud gaming in general, and in particular, why both have struggled to gain a widespread audience over the years. Amazon with Luna, Google with Stadia, and Microsoft with Xbox Cloud Gaming have all tried and failed to achieve breakout success.

“I was at Xbox when we were pushing out X Cloud,” Gattis said. “I think part of the problem is cloud gaming was sort of positioned at core gamers as you don't need a console. There were marketing campaigns around no console required. And in many ways I think that the core gamer who's invested in a console, who's invested in a $3,000 graphics card, not only is committed to that hardware, they love that hardware. They love that fidelity.

"So I think part of it was a product market fit problem where we were marketing clouds, and I mean collectively as an industry, at the wrong people, whereas I think there is a much broader audience that will probably never own a console or never own a game PC and never get a chance to play a lot of these games. That's where I believe in the cloud.”

Not only does Gattis now think that the right audience is being catered to with cloud gaming, but that the tech has caught up with the ambitions of the platforms. “The technology's only getting better,” he insisted. “Several years ago, you would notice latency in certain people’s connections, and you just weren't getting the fidelity that you needed. A lot of that has been removed. So now it's almost like you have to rebuild trust in people who had a bad cloud experience five years ago.”

In terms of Luna, specifically, Gattis believes its current level of popularity is down to how it was positioned when it first arrived on the scene. “I'd say Luna in some ways was trying to compete at the high end of the market with the notion that cloud gaming is just magically going to happen,” he said.

“And when it does, everybody's going to come to Luna and start turning in their consoles and their PCs,” he continued. “That hasn't happened yet. I'd argue if that does happen, they're not automatically going to jump ship from Xbox and PlayStation's team.

“That market is extremely well served. One might even argue it's overserved today where they're all just competing for the same customers, same players; the pie's not really growing. Let's not compete. They can have that at least for now. But what we saw was a broader opportunity where Amazon, we think, can add real value. 3 billion people in the world play games; only about 500 million own consoles and PCs. So we have a lot of people out there that actually like to play video games, but aren't playing in the highest fidelity setting, aren't playing in a living room on a big TV or on a PC monitor.

"We've taken all these games that were previously in a premium subscription with Luna, and we've taken most of them and pushed them all into our standard tier of Luna, which effectively is a Prime benefit. So there's literally close to 100 games in Prime right now that if we're one of the 100 million Prime members worldwide, we have access to all of this. So part of our big challenge is, how do we actually let people know they have this benefit?”

Gattis explained how Luna’s integration into Prime Video will, in theory, aid discoverability: “You launch Prime Video to watch your favorite show, there'll be a games tab right on the top, and that's all the Luna content that you're entitled to be there for you. And so that's a first step in terms of just driving more awareness, and hundreds of millions of people use that app and watch video there."

“And so you can imagine this future where you're going to go to a page, say in Prime Video, and instead of it just being a bunch of things you can click on and play, it's almost a fandom type page," he continued. "If you're a fan of Tomb Raider, here's the show, here's the TV show, here's the game, here's past games, here's a Twitch feed, here's merchandise you can go buy on Amazon.com. So I think that's the vision for us where you start to bring all these things together and think more of general entertainment as opposed to video games being this entirely separate thing from other views.”

This synergy between Amazon’s video game, movie, and TV show output is something Gattis clearly sees as a big part of turning Luna into a success story.

“I fundamentally believe you're seeing a continued intersection between TV video and video games, interactive entertainment,” he said. “So I really think of the future, you'll see every TV or movie is going to have a video game story attached to it, whether that's a AAA game or just some sort of extension of the experience. items.title: Resident Evil Director Zach Cregger Reveals Star Austin Abrams Almost Died Shooting That Zombie Scene From the Trailer
items.description: Zach Cregger has revealed fresh details on the making of the upcoming Resident Evil movie, including a scene where star Austin Abrams almost died from a falling zombie.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Zach Cregger has revealed fresh details on the making of the upcoming Resident Evil movie, including a scene where star Austin Abrams almost died from a falling zombie.

The Barbarian and Weapons creator spoke at a Resident Evil footage screening and Q&A, attended by IGN. There he discussed a scene in which main character Bryan, a medical courier played by Weapons star Austin Abrams, runs down a street as zombies leap down from the roof of buildings on either side. We see this scene briefly in the Resident Evil trailer, below.

During the Q&A, Cregger described how this was shot, and the near miss that might have actually killed the movie’s star.

“We had to basically design this thing where he’s just running and bodies are just falling and detonating all around him. I knew I didn’t want to do it with VFX because I felt like it would just look like VFX. So I was like, how do we do this where all these explosions are real?

“And the way to do it is to get a bunch of cranes and you have all these body-sized blood bags, and you rehearse the s**t out of how they’re going to fall and then how fast he’s going to run. And then you just shoot it and you chase him in the camera car. And he’s running and they’re releasing these bags and they're falling and hitting all around him and exploding.

“And one triggered too early and it missed him by inches. And these things are all like 150 pounds. It would’ve killed him. If he had been like one step to the right, he would have died. And it’s in the movie, so it’s f***ing worth it. I was like, pretty stoked! I was like, ‘Oh, could we do that again?’ They’re like, ‘No we can’t do that again, he almost died!”

If that wasn't enough to make Cregger think twice, during the shooting of another scene, which took place in the Czech Republic in the dead of night, he had a moment of genuine existential crisis.

"He goes to this farm and the first thing that happens is, he gets chased and attacked by a dog. And I’m out in the middle of nowhere, it’s freezing cold, I am wrangling a psycho dog to try and do what I want it to do,” he said.

“Working with animals is hard. And this thing was f***ing terrifying. And I was sick. And it was just one of those things where it was just like… I’d been nocturnal for months making a movie that takes place at night, and I'd just run out of gas. And I just remember thinking, I would rather be anywhere in the world but here in the freezing cold trying to get this dog to do what I want it to do.

“But, you know, I think everyone who makes a movie probably has a moment like that.”

Cregger has previously described his take on Resident Evil as "one gigantic sequence" that follows its regular guy protagonist Bryan as he undertakes a perilous journey "like Frodo going into Mordor." It deliberately avoids featuring characters from Capcom's beloved survival horror series, which means no Leon or Claire turning up to save the day. Bryan is the antithesis of the gun-toting, combat-tested characters who often are the protagonists of Resident Evil games.

Cregger has also spoken in the past about the reaction from some Resident Evil fans who had hoped to see a movie based on one of the games itself, or feature characters from the video games. "There’s so many people that clearly really want the video game, meaning the characters and story from the video game, and anything different than that is really not welcomed," he said in the wake of the trailer's release. "I didn’t realize how passionate some people were about that."

During the Q&A he explained why Leon, for example, isn't in the movie, insisting the video games tell the characters' stories better that he would. "I just wanted to make a movie that would celebrate everything I think makes those games so special," Cregger said, "but not cannibalize the stories that those games tell so well. Because I don't think I can tell Leon’s story better than the games tell Leon's story. That feels to me like kind of a losing endeavor.

"But to tell a story that lives in the world of Raccoon City, on the eve of the outbreak, and play by the rules where, like the Umbrella Corporation, the T-virus and all those things are there, but this story just kind of happens over here, that feels like a really fertile place to live."

Cregger's Resident Evil hits theaters September 18, 2026.

items.title: Zach Gilford Confirms He Won’t Return for Criminal Minds Season 20
items.description: In an exclusive interview, Zach Gilford confirms Elias Voit will not return for Criminal Minds Season 20, but pitches a spin-off for the serial killer.
items.author: Michael Peyton
items.content:
Criminal Minds: Evolution’s big bad is finally hanging up his spiders. In the wake of the long-running procedural’s season 19 finale, Zach Gilford — who plays infamous serial killer-turned-Hannibal Lecter-esque informant Elias Voit (who at one point used venomous arachnids to murder his victims) for the Behavioral Analysis Unit — confirms that he won’t be returning next season.

I spoke exclusively with Gilford about this week’s episode, which saw Voit returning one final time to haunt Joe Mantegna’s Rossi before being put away for good. I asked Gilford about where the character fits in his body of work, whether he’d be up for returning to the show to direct, and his thoughts on not returning as Voit.

“Well, it's sad, honestly,” Gilford says. “Who knows if I ever do come back, but I think Voit is kind of always going to be that white whale not just for Rossi, but the BAU. Even though he's gone, he's still going to be lingering in there somewhere.”

One of Voit’s final scenes saw him popping up as an apparition to Rossi, something that has been part of his character’s arc for multiple seasons. Gilford says that, although he wishes he were coming back for Season 20, it was a great way to send off his character.

“I think it's the right way to do it,” Gilford says. “Because however their relationship has evolved, the last voice that Rossi hears is [Voit] giving him shit. You're like, ‘Oh, you think you're going to get rid of me that easily? That's not happening.’”

Gilford says that if he ever does get to return to the world of Criminal Minds, he has a superhero-inspired idea for a spin-off.

“I've been pitching,” Gilford says. “I think we should just do a spin-off of my character and make it kind of like a Suicide Squad thing. [Voit is] clearly smarter than everyone in the BAU. They haven't solved a fucking crime in four years without me. There are no real plans for me to come back, but I'll jump at it in a heartbeat, as long as it felt not too contrived.”

Gilford, who’s directed two episodes of Criminal Minds, also says he’d love to return to the show to helm more episodes.

“Oh my God, I'd love to go back and direct,” Gilford says. “I'd just love to be on that set. Directing was so fun. I love our crew. Everyone works so hard and they're just excited to be there. It's fun directing on a show where you're a cast member because everyone's rooting for you. I'm a hyper-functioning control freak, so directing is a perfect job for [me].”

Gilford — whose other roles include the TV adaptation of Friday Night Lights as loveable quarterback Matt Saracen and in Mike Flanagan's Midnight Mass as the protagonist Riley Flynn — says that he doesn’t see Voit as an aberration on a resumé filled with characters of all stripes.

“I just like playing people who are interesting and complex,” Gilford says. “Matt Saracen is the epitome of a good guy. But what made him that was he was this kid who had too much on his shoulders and he was doing his best. He was failing at times but he was just trying to figure it out.

“I think one of my favorite roles I've played outside [Criminal Minds and] Friday Night Lights would be in Midnight Mass. [That character is a] kind of tortured person who doesn't know what to do with his life and, much like Voit, is saddled with this guilt of his sins. I don't like playing one-dimensional characters. And that's why I think Voit was so cool, because as much as he's the most prolific serial killer ever, he has a heart and he's struggling with it.”

Despite exiting Criminal Minds, Gilford says he feels lucky to be attached to yet another long-running character, even if that meant performing for four seasons as a serial killer.

“I’ve always said, as an actor, the first goal is to work. If you're super lucky you have a role that resonates with people and people know you for. I got that with Friday Night Lights and I think it's cool to have another one with Criminal Minds. It's just cool and it just makes you feel like, ‘Okay, I did good.’”

Criminal Minds: Evolution is streaming now on Paramount+.

items.title: Family Guy Spinoff Stewie Cast Includes Seth MacFarlane, Seth MacFarlane, and Kenan Thompson
items.description: The cast of Family Guy spinoff Stewie has been announced, and it contains SNL stalwart Kenan Thompson, as well as several roles for Seth MacFarlane.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
The cast of Family Guy spinoff Stewie has been announced, and it contains SNL stalwart Kenan Thompson, as well as several roles for Seth MacFarlane.

Family Guy creator MacFarlane will of course be reprising his role as Stewie, in this new series about the world-conquering toddler's adventures at kindergarten. MacFarlane will also voice Bean, a classmate who Variety reported will say very little as he was "dropped on his head one too many times."

Another Family Guy alumni, Mike Henry, has also joined the cast. Known for previously playing Cleveland Brown, Henry will now voice BJ, son of Family Guy's ear-ring wearing Bruce Straight (who he also voices). Kenan Thompson, meanwhile, will voice yet another classmate. Named as Royal, they are described as having "a 'Hell no' attitude about the hazards of Stewie's adventures."

Other roles will be played by The Rookie's Melissa O'Neil (who voices Wanda, on whom Stewie will have a crush) and Aaron Lee as Skunk, the kindergarten class' 100-year-old turtle. There's no mention of loyal Family Guy dog Brian there — a character with whom Stewie has formed a close friendship with over the years, though Deadline previously reported that he will make recurring appearances.

"After getting the boot from his old preschool, Stewie is forced to enrol in a new one that's not exactly top-of-the-line," reads a synopsis. "It's attended by a handful of kids he doesn't know, an elderly class turtle with a half-cocked theory on just about everything, and a teacher who probably shouldn't be allowed anywhere near kids.

"Stewie's miserable, the other kids are miserable, even the turtle is miserable... until Stewie begins rolling out his trusty array of devices to take them anywhere in space and time, turning every boring day at school into an insane and unforgettable adventure."

Stewie is set to debut at some point during the 2027-2028 TV season, and already has a 2-season order. MacFarlane is credited as a co-creator and executive producer on the series, though it will be showrun by veteran Family Guy writer Kirker Butler.

Butler has written episodes of Family Guy for more than 20 years, including its popular Empire Strikes Back parody Something, Something, Something Dark Side, plus various episodes of Family Guy's other spinoff, the now-concluded The Cleveland Show, as well as Only Murders in the Building.

items.title: After Star Fox's Launch and Zelda: Ocarina of Time's Announcement, Miyamoto Defends Nintendo's Recent Spate of Remakes and Says They Lead to 'Future Developments'
items.description: Nintendo legend Shigeru Miyamoto has defended the company's remakes, and said that newer versions of classic titles can lead to "future developments" — something that fans are keen to see for Star Fox and Zelda.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Nintendo legend Shigeru Miyamoto has defended the company's remakes, and said that newer versions of classic titles can lead to "future developments" — something that fans are keen to see for Star Fox and Zelda.

While Nintendo remaking and re-releasing its classic games is absolutely nothing new, it's fair to point out that two of the company's biggest Switch 2 games this year will be very familiar to long-term fans. Star Fox, which launched last month, sparked conversation online for technically being the company's third reimaging of its N64 classic. The upcoming Switch 2 incarnation of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, meanwhile, will follow various re-releases of the N64 original, as well as its 3DS port.

Now, speaking to Japanese gaming magazine Famitsu (via Nintendo Everything), Miyamoto has addressed the claim that there are too many Nintendo remakes — and hinted that the projects will subsequently serve as the basis for something new.

"Some people might say there are a lot of remakes, but after five years, a lot of people have outgrown games and stop playing them," Miyamoto said. "Young people today don't have the opportunity to play games from 10 years ago, so remaking them to be more playable and releasing them again is a good way to meet the demand.

"Letting people know the original games also leads to future developments," he teased, "so we've been actively pursuing that recently."

Following the appearance of Fox McCloud in this year's Super Mario Galaxy Movie, as well as the Switch 2's Star Fox remake, many fans expect an all-new Star Fox game to follow in due course. As for Zelda, it is inevitable that a full-blown follow-up to Tears of the Kingdom is in the works, while Ocarina of Time launches later this year to keep fans busy.

After a major leak and much fan speculation, Nintendo finally confirmed it was remaking Ocarina of Time during last month's major Nintendo Direct. An initial teaser revealed little, though showed the game's 3D art style and confirmed it will launch sometime later in 2026. However, a now-removed product description has hinted that the game will likely be a faithful remake.

Photo by Amy Sussman/Getty Images.

items.title: Sony Knew Killing Discs Would Be 'An Enormous PR Issue' and Had 'Strictest' Guidelines to Gag Staff From Commenting on Controversy, Former God of War Dev Claims
items.description: Sony knew its decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs would spark outrage, and reportedly issued staff with the "strictest" social media guidelines to stop them from publicly commenting on the controversy.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Sony knew its decision to kill PlayStation 5 discs would spark outrage, and reportedly issued staff with the "strictest" social media guidelines to stop them from publicly commenting on the controversy.

That's according to God of War Laufey writer Alanah Pearce, who alleged in a new YouTube video that the restrictions were the most stringent that PlayStation staff had seen — as Sony anticipated its announcement to cause significant blowback.

Earlier this month, Sony stunned fans by announcing that it would stop launching PlayStation 5 games on physical discs from January 2026 onwards. While the move follows a gradual shift in video game sales from boxed copies to digital downloads over the past decade, gamers who prefer to own a physical edition, or who are concerned by the impact this will have on game preservation, have been vocal in their opposition.

Sony's rationale for ditching discs is that it's simply following consumer trends. "In response to shifting trends in consumer preference, new games will be released on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only," Sid Shuman, Senior Director, Sony Interactive Entertainment Content Communications, said in a post on PlayStation Blog.

"As consumer preferences and the broader entertainment industry continue to shift away from physical discs to digital, physical game disc production for all new games releasing on PlayStation consoles will be discontinued starting January 2028. Following this date, new games will be available on PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only. This transition has no impact on games that already released, or will be releasing, prior to January 2028 in disc format.

"This is a natural direction for Sony Interactive Entertainment to adapt to consumer trends as the general preference for digital media significantly outpaces physical discs. This transition will enable us to align more closely with how most of our community prefers to access and play games today."

Despite a high-profile petition and a constant stream of comments on Sony's subsequent livestreams and social media posts — even overshadowing the release of new games that have nothing to do with the controversy — there's been no sign that the PlayStation maker will change its mind. For now, Sony simply hasn't commented further — and is unlikely to do so, Pearce suggested.

"Sony already knew everyone would be pissed off," Pearce began. "They knew this. People working at PlayStation first-party studios told me that Sony had the strictest social media guidelines for this particular thing that they've ever seen issued.

"Sony does somewhat regularly tell employees what they can or can't say about certain things," she explained. "I was under a lot of guidelines when I was working on God of War Laufey. I still am, and they did send me guidelines regarding what I could say on the day that the game was announced. But in this instance, it is apparently the strictest the employees I spoke to have sever seen regarding public communications. They would only have done this if they knew it was going to be an enormous PR issue. This is no surprise to them."

For Sony, going all-digital for new game releases will earn it more money from every sale at a time when console sales are expected to plummet due to their rising costs. For a first-party PlayStation game such as The Last of Us, Sony will only keep around 65% of the money from a physical copy, with around 30% going to the retailer and roughly another 5% on manufacturing costs. Meanwhile, for a physical copy of a third-party game such as the Activision-published Call of Duty, Sony will get a licensing fee, likely around 15%. For digital sales, Sony keeps 100% of first-party game revenue, and a far better cut from third-party titles.

More than 335,000 people have now signed the Change.org petition calling on Sony to U-turn on its decision, though Pearce said that this would not prompt Sony to change its mind. Speaking to IGN, analysts have all said similar. Dr. Serkan Toto, CEO of Japanese game industry consultancy firm Kantan Games, suggested that even if half a million people cancelled their PlayStation Plus subscription in protest, it would be just a drop in the ocean for Sony.

"I sympathize with physical media fans, but Sony will not reverse this decision," Toto told IGN. "They of course knew what the online reaction would look like, and they now wait for this storm to pass.

"Sony has over 120 million active PlayStation users," he continued. "Around 50 million people subscribe to PlayStation Plus. As a thought experiment, let's say 500,000 cancel in protest, that would be just 1% of that business gone — of course not enough for Sony to start rethinking. Digital is just too lucrative."

Image credit: Jaap Arriens/NurPhoto via Getty Images.

items.title: For One Night Only is a New Showcase Celebrating UK Video Game Talent, Here’s How To Watch.
items.author: George Forsyth-Nash
items.content:
The UK has a proud history of creating iconic video game franchises and is home to world-renowned developers ⁠– now, a new major showcase event, For One Night Only, is shining a light on the world-class games made by British studios.

Throughout its approximately 60-80 minute livestream, For One Night Only will feature new trailers, exclusive reveals and on-stage interviews with some of the UK’s biggest and best games industry talent. With a lineup that includes IO Interactive, Team 17 and Criterion (just to name a few), it's easy to see why the UK continues to be a games industry powerhouse.

How to Watch For One Night Only

Join in and celebrate the UK video game industry by watch For One Night Only on Wednesday, 29th July at 7PM BST / 11AM PST via the following platforms:

IGN

YouTube

Facebook

X

Twitch

Steam

What to Expect From For One Night Only

Hosted by comedian Bec Hill in front of a VIP industry audience at Outernet in London’s West End, For One Night Only will feature a mix of exclusive reveals, trailers and never-before-seen interviews from both industry titans and indie talent.

A selection of the developers and publishers, and the games they are showcasing include: Annapurna Interactive with The Lost Wild and Silent Hill: Townfall, Bandai Namco with Little Nightmares 3, IO Interactive with 007 First Light and Yogscast Games with PlateUp!.

For One Night Only will also be supported by a special Steam sale featuring participating British video game studios. The FONO Steam sale starts at 6PM BST on 29th July and runs for one week, so you can make a saving when jumping in to the games featured in the show!

items.title: First Look at Warhammer Blood Bowl, the Free Overhaul for Blood Bowl 3 Due Out Fall 2026
items.description: Warhammer Blood Bowl hits the end zone this fall, and we've got first-look screenshots and confirmed platforms for launch.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Warhammer Blood Bowl hits the end zone this fall, and we've got first-look screenshots and confirmed platforms for launch.

The video game adaptation of Games Workshop’s Warhammer fantasy football tabletop game is now in the hands of Warhammer 40,000: Battlesector publisher Slitherine, which obtained the licence, publishing rights, and back catalog from the collapsing Nacon.

Now, Slitherine has re-announced Warhammer Blood Bowl with a batch of screenshots, below. It’s due out this fall across PC, Xbox, and PlayStation.

Slitherine said Warhammer Blood Bowl is “built upon the solid foundations of Blood Bowl 3,” with series developer Cyanide still in place. The game will also adopt the latest official tabletop ruleset, updated through September 2025 (also known as Third Season Edition). The roster expands with the Bretonnians and Khemri Tomb Kings.

"At Slitherine, we're strategy gamers first and foremost, and Blood Bowl has always been one of our favorite tabletop games," said Marco Alessandro Minoli, Director of Publishing at Slitherine.

"We're incredibly proud to welcome this iconic franchise into our portfolio and to be working alongside the talented team at Cyanide. Our goal with Warhammer Blood Bowl is simple: we want this to become the definitive Blood Bowl video game — not just at launch, but for years to come. Our vision is to support and expand it over time, turning it into a living, constantly evolving experience, just as we've successfully done with other Warhammer titles such as Warhammer 40,000: Battlesector and Warhammer 40,000: Gladius."

Helpfully, everyone who owns Blood Bowl 3 on PC and consoles will receive Warhammer Blood Bowl as a free upgrade, keeping all previously purchased teams and cosmetics. A playable demo is set for the end of the summer on PC. It includes Rumble Mode, a fast-paced, dynamic 7-player format designed for quicker matches.

Blood Bowl 3 has a 'mixed' user review rating on Steam, and it's fair to say the game failed to meet fan expectations when it launched in 2023. IGN's Blood Bowl 3 review returned a 5/10. We said: "Blood Bowl 3 is a sloppy, muddy, buggy rehash of a better game."

items.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power is Finally Introducing Galadriel's Husband Celeborn — And a Famous Face From Stranger Things is Playing Her 'Lover-Boy' Beau
items.description: Galadriel's husband Celeborn will finally be introduced in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, with new episodes set to debut Stranger Things' Jamie Campbell Bower as her "lover-boy" partner.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Galadriel's husband Celeborn will finally be introduced in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, with new episodes set to debut Stranger Things' Jamie Campbell Bower as her "lover-boy" partner.

Exactly how Celeborn will be introduced — and where he's supposed to have been for the past two seasons — remains under wraps. But Empire has confirmed that Celeborn will feature in the show's upcoming third season, and that the actor behind Stranger Things' Vecna will play Galadriel's fair-headed fellow.

As Tolkien fans will know, Galadriel and Celeborn were married during Middle-earth's First Age, long prior to the events of the Second Age, which The Rings of Power is adapting. In the show's first season, Galadriel mentions that her husband never returned from fighting Morgoth — with the implication being that she has not seen him since.

Until now, our only glimpses of Celeborn on screen come from a couple of cameo appearances in Peter Jackson's The Lord of the Rings trilogy. But not to worry if you can't really remember him — he has very little to do, with Galadriel herself very much the star.

"This idea of longing and yearning is so pervasive in Tolkien's relationship with [his wife] Edith for the time that they were apart," Bower said of Celeborn and Galadriel's relationship, which is inspired by the author's long absences from his own wife during youth and while fighting in the First World War. "I really feasted on that idea. Celeborn has had to find a way to survive whilst longing for something that he so dearly loved and so dearly missed as well."

Bower described his character's demeanour as a "lover-boy," while Galadriel actress Morfydd Clark noted that her elf alter ego was "kind of rude to him in the books."

"She's the queen!" Clark concluded. "But Jamie looks exactly like how I would imagine Celeborn. He's such an elf."

Rings of Power is set to debut its third season via Prime Video at some point before the end of 2026 — a two-year wait for fans since the show's last episode. But while it may have been a couple of years for fans, it will have been even longer for Rings of Power's characters — who'll after something of a time jump. While Season 2 ended with Galadriel and her elvish friends finally united and ready to fight the growing threat of Sauron, the series' third run will fast forward to the middle of the subsequent conflict.

"Jumping forward several years from the events of Season 2, Season 3 takes place at the height of the War of the Elves and Sauron," an official synopsis reads, "as the Dark Lord seeks to craft the One Ring that will give him the edge he needs to win the war and conquer all Middle-earth at last."

Earlier this year, it was reported that Rings of Power was still on-track to run for five seasons, with the $1 billion Prime Video show claimed to be still under the protection of Amazon boss Jeff Bezos' "magical halo" despite its huge costs.

Image credit: Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images.

items.title: Xbox Gamers Slam Paramount After Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game Suffers Shock Delay on Their Console Just Hours Before Launch
items.description: Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game has suffered a shock delay on Xbox just hours before it was due to come out, sparking a backlash from fans.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game has suffered a shock delay on Xbox just hours before it was due to come out, sparking a backlash from fans.

The Paramount Games Studio-published fighting game, developed by Gameplay Group International, was due out today, July 23, across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, PC via Steam, and Nintendo Switch.

But in a note to fans published just a few hours ago, Paramount said the Switch version will be available as the Standard Edition only, and crossplay with other platforms and language localization beyond English will not be available. “We are committed to bringing these features, along with upgrading to Deluxe Edition, to players as soon as possible and will keep you updated on our timeline and progress,” Paramount said.

But it’s an even worse situation for Xbox fans, who have seen the game in its entirety delayed to September 3 — a 6-week wait that sets Xbox players back significantly on the competitive front. Paramount failed to say exactly what the issue was, speaking in vague terms to say it was due to “unforeseen circumstances on a backend feature.”

“For the Xbox community, we are forced to delay the release,” Paramount said. “Due to unforeseen circumstances on a backend feature, we will now launch by September 3. Existing preorders will remain active and will not be canceled.

“Our priority is delivering the best possible experience on every platform and we are working tirelessly to make that happen. Thank you for your patience, understanding and continued support. We’re excited to get everyone into the fight as soon as possible. Tune in here for updates as we have them.”

As you’d expect, Xbox gamers have reacted negatively to the news, with many of the replies highly critical of Paramount.

“F**k your game!” replied one person. “Delaying your game HOURS before release on XBOX is horrible management. Zero excuses. You should’ve known this WELL IN ADVANCE. Keep your game, not buying it. Was looking forward to it so much as an Avatar TLA fan.”
